offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (BAC .15+); Level 6 Felony (prior within 7 years or minor passenger); Level 5 Felony (serious injury); Level 4 Felony (death)
penalty_max: 60 days (Class C Misd); 1 year (Class A Misd); 2.5 years (Level 6); 6 years (Level 5); 12 years (Level 4)
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle
While intoxicated — BAC of .08 or higher, or with a controlled substance in blood
Or while impaired to the point that there is an endangered person
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher (Class A Misdemeanor minimum)
Causing serious bodily injury (Level 5 Felony under § 9-30-5-4)
notes: Indiana uses 'OWI' (Operating While Intoxicated) rather than DUI/DWI. Implied consent under § 9-30-6-1. Refusal results in 1-year license suspension. Specialized driving privileges may be available.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle
While intoxicated with BAC of .08 or higher
No prior OWI convictions within 7 years
mandatory_minimum: Minimum 90-day license suspension; substance abuse evaluation
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher (elevated to Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: First offense with BAC under .15 and no endangerment is a Class C Misdemeanor. Probation common. Court may order ignition interlock device.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle while intoxicated
Defendant has a prior OWI conviction within 7 years
mandatory_minimum: 5 days imprisonment or 240 hours community service
notes: Prior conviction must be within 7 years. Habitual vehicular substance offender status possible under § 9-30-15.5. License suspension 1-2 years.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor; elevated same as alcohol OWI
penalty_max: Same as alcohol OWI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol OWI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle
With a Schedule I or II controlled substance or its metabolite in the defendant's blood
notes: Per se violation — any detectable amount of Schedule I or II substance in blood is sufficient. No impairment proof required. Includes marijuana metabolites.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (if resulting in damage to person or property)
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle
In a reckless manner
That created a substantial risk of bodily injury to another person
enhancements: Resulting in bodily injury or property damage (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Common reduction from OWI charges. Adds points to driving record.

statute_title: Leaving the Scene of an Accident
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (property); Level 6 Felony (injury); Level 5 Felony (serious injury/death)
elements: Defendant was the operator of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop and provide information or render aid
enhancements: Resulting in serious bodily injury (Level 5 Felony)
notes: Duty to stop and provide information under § 9-26-1-1.1. Must give name, address, and vehicle registration. Must render reasonable assistance to injured persons.

offense_class: Level 4 Felony
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle while intoxicated
The operation caused the death of another person
notes: Indiana does not have a separate vehicular homicide statute — OWI causing death is charged under § 9-30-5-5. Non-OWI vehicular deaths may be charged as reckless homicide under § 35-42-1-5.

offense_class: Level 5 Felony
elements: Defendant recklessly killed another human being
enhancements: Committed while operating a vehicle (may also face OWI charges)
notes: Used for non-OWI vehicular deaths involving reckless conduct. Indiana does not use the term 'vehicular manslaughter' — the charge is reckless homicide.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Level 6 Felony (if prior conviction within 10 years or if suspension was OWI-related)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While driving privileges were suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension
notes: Knowledge of suspension is an element. BMV mailing of suspension notice creates rebuttable presumption of knowledge.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony (vehicle used as weapon or causes injury)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally fled from law enforcement
After being ordered to stop
Using a vehicle
enhancements: Vehicle used to commit forcible felony (Level 5 Felony)
notes: Vehicular flight from police is under the resisting law enforcement statute, not a separate traffic statute. Foot pursuit is Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Level 6 Felony (prior conviction or amount enhancement)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a controlled substance
Pure or adulterated
Without a valid prescription
enhancements: Possession in or near school, park, or family housing complex (Level 6 Felony)
notes: Indiana consolidated many possession offenses under § 35-48-4-7. Schedule and amount determine base level. Diversion programs available for first-time offenders.

statute_title: Possession of Marijuana, Hash Oil, Hashish, or Salvia
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (under 30g); Class A Misdemeanor (30g+ or prior); Level 6 Felony (prior + amount)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed marijuana, hash oil, hashish, or salvia
Without a valid prescription or legal authorization
notes: Indiana has not legalized recreational marijuana. Possession of any amount remains criminal. Hash oil is treated more seriously under § 35-48-4-11(b).

statute_title: Possession of Cocaine or a Narcotic Drug
offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony (5g+); Level 4 Felony (10g+); Level 3 Felony (28g+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed cocaine or a narcotic drug
Pure or adulterated
enhancements: Near school, park, or family housing complex
notes: Cocaine is classified as a Schedule II narcotic under Indiana law. Weight thresholds include the full mixture weight, not just pure cocaine.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony (5g+); Level 4 Felony (10g+); Level 3 Felony (28g+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed methamphetamine
Pure or adulterated
enhancements: Near school, park, or family housing complex
notes: Separate statute from general narcotic possession. Same weight thresholds as cocaine. Indiana has enhanced penalties for meth due to manufacturing prevalence.

statute_title: Dealing in Cocaine or a Narcotic Drug
offense_class: Level 5 Felony; Level 4 Felony (5g+); Level 3 Felony (10g+); Level 2 Felony (28g+ or death results)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally manufactured, delivered, or financed the delivery of cocaine or a narcotic drug
Or possessed with intent to manufacture, deliver, or finance the delivery
enhancements: Near school, park, or family housing complex
notes: Indiana uses 'dealing' rather than 'trafficking.' Separate statutes exist for different drug types (§ 35-48-4-1 through 35-48-4-4.6).

statute_title: Dealing in a Schedule I, II, or III Controlled Substance
offense_class: Level 6 Felony; enhanced by amount and circumstances
penalty_max: 2.5 years (Level 6); up to 30 years with enhancements
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally manufactured, delivered, or financed the delivery of a Schedule I, II, or III substance
Or possessed with intent to deliver
enhancements: Near school, park, or family housing complex
notes: Covers dealing in controlled substances not specifically addressed by cocaine/meth/marijuana dealing statutes.

offense_class: Level 4 Felony; Level 3 Felony (prior or near children); Level 2 Felony (causing death/serious injury)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally manufactured or attempted to manufacture methamphetamine
enhancements: Manufacturing in presence of child (Level 3 Felony)
notes: Indiana has specific meth manufacturing statute due to prevalence. Other drug manufacturing falls under general dealing statutes. Environmental cleanup costs may be assessed.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (prior or syringe)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed an instrument, device, or object
Used or intended to be used to introduce a controlled substance into the body
Or to test the strength, analyze, or facilitate the use of a controlled substance
enhancements: Syringe possession (Class A Misdemeanor under § 35-48-4-8.5, with exceptions for needle exchange)
notes: Indiana has a separate syringe possession statute. Needle exchange program participants are exempt under certain conditions.

statute_title: Possession of Cocaine/Narcotic with Intent to Deliver
offense_class: Level 5 Felony; enhanced by weight
penalty_max: 6 years (Level 5); up to 30 years with weight enhancements
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed cocaine or a narcotic drug
With intent to manufacture, deliver, or finance the delivery
enhancements: Near school, park, or family housing complex
notes: Intent to deliver is often inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, large amounts of cash, and other circumstantial evidence.

offense_class: Murder (45-65 years); possible LWOP or death sentence
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally killed another human being
notes: Indiana does not use 'degrees' for murder. There is one murder statute. The sentencing range is 45-65 years, with LWOP or death for aggravated cases. Indiana retains the death penalty.

statute_title: Murder — Felony Murder / Killing While Committing a Felony
offense_class: Murder (45-65 years)
elements: Defendant killed another human being

While committing or attempting to commit arson, burglary, child molesting, criminal deviate conduct, kidnapping, rape, robbery, carjacking, criminal gang activity, or dealing in a controlled substance
enhancements: Life without parole where aggravating circumstances exist
notes: Indiana's felony murder rule. Same penalty range as intentional murder. No separate 'second degree murder' — this is the felony murder provision within the single murder statute.

offense_class: Level 2 Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally killed another human being
While acting under sudden heat
notes: 'Sudden heat' is a mitigating factor that reduces murder to voluntary manslaughter. The defendant bears the burden of proving sudden heat. It is not a defense, but a sentencing reduction.

offense_class: Level 5 Felony
elements: Defendant killed another human being
While committing or attempting to commit a Class A misdemeanor or Level 6 felony that is inherently dangerous
Or while committing a Class A misdemeanor involving operation of a vehicle with at least one prior OWI
notes: Involuntary manslaughter in Indiana requires a predicate offense. Simple negligence causing death is not sufficient without an underlying misdemeanor or felony.

offense_class: Level 3 Felony; Level 1 Felony (if victim under 14 or involving deadly weapon causing serious injury)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally inflicted injury on another person
That created a substantial risk of death
Or caused serious permanent disfigurement
Or caused the loss or impairment of a bodily organ or function
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon causing serious injury (Level 1 Felony)
notes: Indiana uses 'battery' rather than 'assault' for physical contact offenses. This is the equivalent of aggravated assault in other states.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (resulting in bodily injury); Level 6 Felony (moderate injury or victim is public safety official)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally touched another person
In a rude, insolent, or angry manner
enhancements: Resulting in bodily injury (Class A Misdemeanor)
Resulting in moderate bodily injury (Level 6 Felony)
Against a public safety official (Level 6 Felony)
notes: Indiana's battery statute covers what most states call 'simple assault.' Touching in a rude manner is sufficient — no injury required for the base offense.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally touched another person in a rude, insolent, or angry manner
The touching resulted in bodily injury
notes: Battery resulting in bodily injury is the most commonly charged battery offense. 'Bodily injury' means any impairment of physical condition, including physical pain.

offense_class: Level 5 Felony; Level 3 Felony (resulting in bodily injury); Level 2 Felony (serious bodily injury)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally took property from another person
By using or threatening the use of force
Or by putting the victim in fear
enhancements: Resulting in serious bodily injury (Level 2 Felony)
Armed with a deadly weapon (Level 3 Felony)
notes: Robbery requires force or threat of force. Taking property without force is theft, not robbery.

offense_class: Level 3 Felony; Level 2 Felony (serious injury)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally took property from another person
By using or threatening the use of force
While armed with a deadly weapon
enhancements: Resulting in serious bodily injury (Level 2 Felony)
notes: Armed robbery is an enhancement within the robbery statute, not a separate offense. 'Deadly weapon' includes firearms, knives, and any object used in a manner that could cause death or serious injury.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony (victim under 14 or disabled); Level 3 Felony (weapon, injury, or ransom); Level 2 Felony (serious injury); Level 1 Felony (victim is under 14 and not a parent)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally removed another person by fraud, enticement, force, or threat of force
From one place to another
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (Level 3 Felony)
Victim under 14 (Level 1 Felony if offender is not parent)
Resulting in serious bodily injury (Level 2 Felony)
notes: Confinement (§ 35-42-3-3) is a lesser included offense. Criminal confinement does not require movement, while kidnapping does.

offense_class: Level 4 Felony; Level 3 Felony (dwelling or risk to human life); Level 2 Felony (serious injury); Level 1 Felony (death)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally set fire to or burned property
By means of fire or explosive
With intent to damage or destroy
enhancements: Dwelling or property with persons inside (Level 3 Felony)
Resulting in serious bodily injury (Level 2 Felony)
notes: Arson of a dwelling is automatically Level 3 regardless of whether anyone is home. Insurance fraud arson carries additional charges.

offense_class: Level 1 Felony
elements: Defendant, acting with the culpability required for murder
Engaged in conduct that constituted a substantial step toward the commission of murder
enhancements: Use of a firearm (additional fixed term under § 35-50-2-11)
notes: Attempted murder is one level below the base murder charge. Penalty range is the advisory range for a Level 1 Felony.

offense_class: Level 5 Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally touched another person
In a rude, insolent, or angry manner
With a deadly weapon
enhancements: Resulting in serious bodily injury (Level 3 Felony or higher)
notes: Indiana charges this as battery with a deadly weapon, not 'assault with a deadly weapon.' A deadly weapon includes firearms, knives, and anything used in a manner that could cause death.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Level 6 Felony ($750+); Level 5 Felony ($50,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally exerted unauthorized control over property of another person
With intent to deprive the other person of any part of the property's value or use
enhancements: Prior theft conviction (Level 6 Felony regardless of amount)
notes: Indiana's unified theft statute covers larceny, embezzlement, and theft of services. The $750 felony threshold is relatively low compared to many states.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony ($750-$49,999); Level 5 Felony ($50,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally exerted unauthorized control over property
With intent to deprive the owner of value or use
Value of property is $750 or more
notes: Indiana does not use the term 'grand theft.' This is felony-level theft based on the $750 threshold.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally exerted unauthorized control over property
With intent to deprive the owner of value or use
Value of property is under $750
enhancements: Prior theft conviction (Level 6 Felony regardless of amount)
notes: Misdemeanor theft. Prior theft conviction elevates any theft to Level 6 Felony regardless of value. Diversion programs may be available.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $750); Level 6 Felony ($750+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally exerted unauthorized control over property of a retail establishment
With intent to deprive the retailer of value
notes: Shoplifting is charged under the general theft statute. Retailers may also pursue civil recovery under § 34-24-3-1 (up to $150 plus actual damages).

offense_class: Level 5 Felony; Level 4 Felony (dwelling); Level 3 Felony (armed or injury); Level 2 Felony (dwelling + armed or injury); Level 1 Felony (serious injury)
elements: Defendant broke and entered the building or structure of another person
With intent to commit a felony or theft therein
enhancements: Armed with a deadly weapon (Level 3 Felony)
Resulting in serious bodily injury (Level 1 Felony)
notes: Indiana requires 'breaking and entering' — mere entry through an open door may not qualify. Intent to commit a felony must exist at the time of entry.

offense_class: Level 4 Felony; Level 2 Felony (armed or injury)
elements: Defendant broke and entered the dwelling of another person
With intent to commit a felony or theft therein
enhancements: Armed with a deadly weapon (Level 2 Felony)
Resulting in serious bodily injury (Level 1 Felony)
notes: Dwelling burglary is automatically elevated to Level 4. A 'dwelling' is a building or structure used for lodging.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally exerted unauthorized control over a motor vehicle of another person
With intent to deprive the owner
enhancements: Value $50,000 or more (Level 5 Felony under general theft statute)
notes: Indiana has a specific auto theft statute. Carjacking (taking by force) is charged as robbery, not auto theft.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $750); Level 6 Felony ($750+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally received, retained, or disposed of property of another person
That had been the subject of theft
Knowing or having reason to believe the property was stolen
notes: Receiving stolen property is included within Indiana's consolidated theft statute. The 'reason to believe' standard is objective.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor ($750+); Level 6 Felony ($5,000+ or substantial risk)
elements: Defendant recklessly, knowingly, or intentionally damaged or defaced property of another person
Without the other person's consent
enhancements: Damage $5,000+ or substantial risk to human life (Level 6 Felony)
notes: Indiana uses 'criminal mischief' for property destruction/vandalism. Graffiti falls under this statute.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Level 6 Felony (dwelling, prior, or with weapon)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally entered the property of another person
After having been denied entry
Or refused to leave after being asked
notes: Criminal trespass requires notice — posting of signs, verbal warning, or fencing. Trespass on agricultural land has specific provisions.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor ($750+); Level 6 Felony ($5,000+)
elements: Defendant recklessly, knowingly, or intentionally damaged or defaced property of another person
Without the other person's consent
notes: Criminal mischief is Indiana's primary property damage/vandalism statute. Restitution is typically ordered in addition to criminal penalties.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Level 6 Felony (prior or in presence of child under 16); Level 5 Felony (serious injury or deadly weapon)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally touched a family or household member
In a rude, insolent, or angry manner
Resulting in bodily injury
enhancements: Committed in the presence of a child under 16 (Level 6 Felony)
Resulting in serious bodily injury (Level 5 Felony)
Committed with a deadly weapon (Level 5 Felony)
notes: Indiana has a specific domestic battery statute separate from general battery. 'Family or household member' includes spouses, former spouses, co-parents, and cohabitants. Mandatory arrest policy for officers responding to domestic calls.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Level 6 Felony (prior or child present)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally touched a family or household member
In a rude, insolent, or angry manner
Resulting in bodily injury
notes: Same statute as domestic violence entry. Federal firearms prohibition applies upon conviction (18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(9)).

offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony (bodily injury); Level 3 Felony (serious injury); Level 1 Felony (death)
elements: Defendant had the care of a dependent (child under 14, endangered adult)
Defendant knowingly or intentionally placed the dependent in a situation that endangered their life or health
enhancements: Resulting in serious bodily injury (Level 3 Felony)
notes: Indiana uses 'neglect of a dependent' rather than 'child endangerment.' Covers both children and dependent adults. Includes leaving a child in a hot car, exposure to drug manufacturing, etc.

offense_class: Level 5 Felony; Level 3 Felony (serious injury); Level 1 Felony (aggravated battery against child under 14)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally touched a person under 14
In a rude, insolent, or angry manner
Resulting in bodily injury
enhancements: Aggravated battery against child under 14 (Level 1 Felony under § 35-42-2-1.5)
notes: Battery against a child under 14 resulting in injury is automatically a Level 5 Felony. DCS investigation typically accompanies criminal charges.

statute_title: Invasion of Privacy (Violation of Protective Order)
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Level 6 Felony (prior or with threat/weapon)
elements: A protective order was issued against the defendant
Defendant knowingly or intentionally violated the order
enhancements: Prior conviction for invasion of privacy (Level 6 Felony)
Committed with a deadly weapon or threat of deadly force (Level 6 Felony)
notes: Indiana calls protective order violations 'invasion of privacy.' The protective order must be properly served. Contact through third parties can constitute a violation.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony (threat of violence, prior, or protective order in effect); Level 4 Felony (weapon or victim under 16)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally engaged in a course of conduct
Directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, or threatened
The victim was actually terrorized, frightened, intimidated, or threatened
enhancements: Implicit or explicit threat of violence (Level 5 Felony)
notes: Stalking requires a 'course of conduct' — a pattern of repeated acts. A single incident is generally insufficient. Cyberstalking is included.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (threat of violence)
elements: Defendant, with intent to harass, annoy, or alarm another person
Made a telephone call, sent electronic communication, or engaged in conduct
With no purpose of legitimate communication
notes: Harassment requires specific intent — accidental or incidental contact is not sufficient. Includes repeated unwanted phone calls, texts, and social media messages.

statute_title: Exploitation of a Dependent or Endangered Adult
offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony ($50,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally exploited an endangered adult or dependent
By improperly using or managing the finances, property, or resources of the person
enhancements: Value of exploitation $50,000 or more (Level 5 Felony)
notes: Physical abuse of an elder is charged under battery or neglect of a dependent statutes. This statute specifically covers financial exploitation. 'Endangered adult' is defined in § 12-10-3-2.

statute_title: Carrying a Handgun Without a License
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Level 5 Felony (prior conviction for violent offense)
elements: Defendant carried a handgun
Without a valid license to carry
enhancements: Prior conviction for a violent offense (Level 5 Felony)
notes: Indiana passed a permitless carry law (HEA 1296) effective July 1, 2022, eliminating the license requirement for most adults. This statute still applies to persons disqualified from carrying (felons, certain misdemeanor convicts, minors, etc.).

statute_title: Serious Violent Felon in Possession of a Firearm
offense_class: Level 4 Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a firearm
Defendant is a serious violent felon as defined by § 35-47-4-5
notes: 'Serious violent felon' includes prior convictions for murder, battery with a deadly weapon, robbery, and other specified offenses. Less serious felons who possess firearms may be charged under § 35-47-4-6 (Level 5 Felony).

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Level 5 Felony (if prohibited person)
elements: Defendant carried a handgun
Defendant is a person prohibited from carrying under § 35-47-2-3 (domestic battery conviction, certain drug offenses, adjudicated mentally incompetent)
notes: With Indiana's 2022 permitless carry law, this primarily applies to prohibited persons. Prohibited categories include those convicted of domestic battery within last 7 years, certain drug offenses, and persons under 18.

statute_title: Criminal Recklessness with a Deadly Weapon
offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony (at inhabited dwelling or occupied vehicle)
elements: Defendant recklessly, knowingly, or intentionally performed an act
That created a substantial risk of bodily injury to another person
While armed with a deadly weapon
enhancements: Shooting at an inhabited dwelling or occupied vehicle (Level 5 Felony)
notes: Indiana does not have a specific 'illegal discharge' statute. Reckless discharge of a firearm is charged as criminal recklessness under § 35-42-2-2.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony ($50,000+ loss or victim is vulnerable adult)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally obtained, possessed, transferred, or used the identifying information of another person
Without the other person's consent
With intent to harm or defraud
enhancements: Victim is an endangered adult or dependent (Level 5 Felony)
notes: Indiana uses 'identity deception' rather than 'identity theft.' Synthetic identity fraud (creating a new identity from parts of real identities) is also covered.

offense_class: Same as theft: Class A Misdemeanor to Level 5 Felony based on value
elements: Defendant had lawful possession of property belonging to another
Defendant knowingly or intentionally exerted unauthorized control over the property
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Embezzlement is not a separate statute in Indiana — it falls under the unified theft statute. The key distinguishing element is that the defendant had lawful initial possession.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony
elements: Defendant, with intent to defraud, made, uttered, or possessed a written instrument
Knowing the instrument was falsely made, altered, or that the making was unauthorized
enhancements: Forgery of a financial instrument (Level 6 Felony)
notes: Forgery covers checks, deeds, wills, contracts, and other legal documents. Uttering (presenting a forged document) is included within the forgery statute.

statute_title: Counterfeiting — Forgery of Currency or Government Instrument
offense_class: Level 6 Felony
elements: Defendant made, uttered, or possessed counterfeit currency or government instrument
With intent to defraud
notes: Counterfeiting is primarily a federal offense (18 U.S.C. § 471). State charges under Indiana's forgery statute are less common but do occur for possession of counterfeit bills.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Level 6 Felony ($750+ or multiple incidents)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally made or delivered a check, draft, or money order
Knowing there were insufficient funds or no account to cover it
With intent to defraud
notes: The payee must have accepted the check in exchange for property or services. Post-dated checks with the payee's knowledge are not covered.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally presented or caused to be presented
A false or misleading statement or claim for insurance benefits
With intent to defraud an insurer
notes: Covers auto insurance, health insurance, and property insurance fraud. Indiana Insurance Fraud Unit investigates. Restitution is typically ordered.

statute_title: Fraud on a Financial Institution (Credit Card Fraud)
offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony ($50,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally executed or attempted to execute a scheme to defraud a financial institution
Or obtained money, funds, or credit through false or fraudulent representations
notes: Credit card fraud may also be charged as identity deception (§ 35-43-5-3.5) or theft (§ 35-43-4-2) depending on the circumstances.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony ($50,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally conducted a financial transaction involving proceeds of criminal activity
With intent to conceal or disguise the nature, location, source, ownership, or control of the proceeds
notes: Indiana's money laundering statute applies to proceeds from any criminal activity. Structuring transactions to avoid reporting requirements is also covered.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony ($50,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally made a false or misleading statement
To obtain property, money, or employment
With intent to defraud
notes: General fraud catch-all provision. Specific fraud types (insurance, welfare, identity) have dedicated statutes with potentially different penalty structures.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony
elements: Defendant, with intent to arouse or satisfy sexual desires
Touched another person
When that person was compelled to submit by force or imminent threat of force
enhancements: Use of deadly force or threat (Level 4 Felony)
notes: Sexual battery is Indiana's equivalent of sexual assault in other states. More serious sexual contact offenses are charged as rape under § 35-42-4-1.

offense_class: Level 3 Felony; Level 1 Felony (deadly weapon, serious injury, drugs, or victim is disabled/under 14)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally had sexual intercourse with another person
By using or threatening the use of deadly force
Or when the victim was unaware or lacked mental capacity to consent
Or when the victim was compelled by force or imminent threat of force
enhancements: Use of deadly force or weapon (Level 1 Felony)
Resulting in serious bodily injury (Level 1 Felony)
Administration of drugs without consent (Level 1 Felony)
notes: Indiana's rape statute is gender-neutral. Sex offender registration required upon conviction. Civil commitment as sexually violent predator possible under § 35-38-1-7.5.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Level 6 Felony (prior or child present)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally appeared in a public place
In a state of nudity with intent to be seen
Or engaged in sexual intercourse or other sexual conduct in a public place
notes: Indiana uses 'public indecency' rather than 'indecent exposure.' Repeat offenses or exposure to children triggers sex offender registration requirements.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (patronizing); Level 5 Felony (promoting); Level 4 Felony (victim under 18)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally paid or offered to pay for sexual conduct
Or promoted or profited from prostitution
notes: Patronizing a prostitute is a Class A Misdemeanor. Promoting prostitution (pimping) is a felony. Human trafficking charges apply when force, fraud, or coercion is involved.

offense_class: Level 5 Felony (possession); Level 4 Felony (dissemination)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a depiction of a child engaged in sexual conduct
Or disseminated such material
notes: Each image or video may be charged as a separate count. Sex offender registration required. Federal charges often accompany state charges (18 U.S.C. § 2252).

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony (sexually violent predator)
elements: Defendant is required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly or intentionally failed to register or update registration
notes: Must register within 72 hours of release or change of address. Lifetime registration required for certain offenses. Failure to register is a separate offense from the underlying sex crime.

offense_class: Level 5 Felony (victim 14-15); Level 4 Felony (victim under 14); Level 1 Felony (compulsion, weapon, or serious injury)
elements: Defendant, being at least 18 years old, engaged in sexual intercourse or other sexual conduct
With a person under 16
enhancements: Victim under 14 (Level 4 Felony — charged as child molesting under § 35-42-4-3)
Use of force or weapon (Level 1 Felony)
notes: Indiana's age of consent is 16. 'Romeo and Juliet' provisions may apply when the age difference is small. Offenses against children under 14 are charged as child molesting, a more serious offense.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant recklessly, knowingly, or intentionally engaged in fighting, tumultuous conduct, or unreasonable noise
That disturbed or tended to disturb a lawful assembly of persons
notes: Common charge for bar fights, loud disturbances, and public altercations. Often used as a reduced charge in plea negotiations.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Level 6 Felony (vehicle or force); Level 5 Felony (vehicle causing injury)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally resisted, obstructed, or interfered with a law enforcement officer
While the officer was lawfully engaged in the officer's duties
enhancements: Using a vehicle and causing injury (Level 5 Felony)
notes: Passive resistance (going limp) can be charged. The officer must be acting lawfully — unlawful arrest may be a defense. This is the same statute used for fleeing/eluding.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally induced, by threat, coercion, or deception
A witness or informant to withhold testimony, avoid legal process, or provide false information
Or altered, destroyed, or concealed evidence
notes: Obstruction includes tampering with witnesses, destroying evidence, and providing false information to investigators. Separate from resisting law enforcement.

offense_class: Court-imposed sanctions; may include imprisonment
penalty_max: Discretion of the court — typically up to 180 days for civil contempt; criminal contempt may carry longer terms
elements: A court order existed and was served on the defendant
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully disobeyed the order
notes: Contempt in Indiana is governed by civil procedure rules as well as criminal statutes. Direct contempt (in the judge's presence) can be punished summarily. Indirect contempt requires notice and hearing.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant was in a public place
In a state of intoxication
That was a danger to the defendant or others, or was breaching the peace
notes: Indiana requires the person be a danger to self or others, or breaching the peace — mere public intoxication without additional conduct may be insufficient.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor case); Level 6 Felony (felony case)
elements: Defendant was released on bond or recognizance
Defendant was required to appear at a specified time and place
Defendant knowingly or intentionally failed to appear
enhancements: Underlying case is a felony (Level 6 Felony)
notes: Failure to appear results in a bench warrant. Bond may be forfeited. The FTA charge is in addition to the underlying case.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (false report of emergency)
elements: Defendant gave a false report of the commission of a crime
Or false alarm of fire or other emergency
Knowing the report to be false
enhancements: False report of emergency or bomb threat (Class A Misdemeanor or Level 6 Felony)
notes: Filing a false police report is the most common charge. False emergency calls (swatting) may be charged as a felony.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony; Level 5 Felony (with weapon or threat to commit forcible felony)
elements: Defendant communicated a threat to another person
With the intent that the other person be placed in fear of retaliation for a prior lawful act
Or with the intent to cause the other person to engage in or refrain from specific conduct
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (Level 5 Felony)
Threat to commit a forcible felony (Level 5 Felony)
Directed at a public servant, witness, or juror (Level 5 Felony)
notes: Indiana uses 'intimidation' rather than 'criminal threat.' The threat must be intended to cause fear or compel action — mere angry words without specific intent may be insufficient.

offense_class: Level 6 Felony
elements: Defendant made a false, material statement under oath or affirmation
Knowing the statement to be false
In or in connection with an official proceeding
notes: The statement must be material — false statements on immaterial matters are not perjury. Inconsistent statements under oath may support a perjury charge without proving which statement was false.

offense_class: Level 5 Felony
elements: Defendant conferred or offered to confer a benefit on a public servant
With the intent to influence the public servant's performance of official duties
notes: Both the giver and receiver of a bribe can be charged. Covers all public servants including judges, legislators, and law enforcement officers.

offense_class: Level 5 Felony; Level 4 Felony (using violence)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally escaped from lawful detention
Including removal from a penal facility, transport, or community corrections
notes: Includes walking away from work release, community corrections, or electronic monitoring. Escape from state prison or using violence increases the felony level.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Level 6 Felony (prior, torture, or death of animal)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally tortured, beat, or mutilated a vertebrate animal
Or abandoned or neglected a vertebrate animal
notes: Indiana's animal cruelty laws have been strengthened. Cockfighting and dogfighting carry separate charges under § 35-46-3-8 and § 35-46-3-9.

offense_class: Not a new criminal charge — court may impose any sentence available for the original offense
penalty_max: Up to the maximum sentence for the original offense
fine_max: Up to the maximum fine for the original offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation for a criminal conviction
Defendant violated a condition of probation
The violation must be proved by a preponderance of the evidence
notes: Probation violations use preponderance of evidence standard, not beyond a reasonable doubt. Court has broad discretion — may continue, modify, or revoke probation. Graduated sanctions under § 35-38-2-3(h) may apply.

offense_class: Not a new criminal charge — parole board determines consequences
penalty_max: Return to incarceration for remainder of sentence
elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
notes: Indiana Parole Board handles parole violations. The parolee is entitled to a hearing. Parole may be revoked, modified, or continued. New criminal charges may also apply.

statute_title: Aiding, Inducing, or Causing an Offense
offense_class: Same as the underlying offense
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally aided, induced, or caused another person to commit an offense
notes: An aider is liable to the same extent as the principal. Mere presence at the scene is insufficient — some affirmative act or encouragement is required.

offense_class: One level below the underlying offense (e.g., attempted Level 3 Felony = Level 4 Felony)
penalty_min: Varies based on the level of the underlying offense
penalty_max: Varies — one level below the underlying offense
elements: Defendant, acting with the culpability required for the underlying offense
Engaged in conduct that constituted a substantial step toward the commission of the offense
notes: Attempt is graded one level below the completed offense. A 'substantial step' must strongly corroborate the criminal intent — mere preparation is insufficient. Attempted murder is a Level 1 Felony (exception to the general one-level-below rule).

offense_class: Same level as the underlying offense (felony); Class A Misdemeanor (if underlying is misdemeanor)
penalty_min: Varies by the level of the underlying offense
elements: Defendant, with intent to commit a felony, agreed with another person to commit the felony
Either defendant or co-conspirator performed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement
notes: Conspiracy requires an agreement and an overt act. A person cannot conspire alone — there must be at least two co-conspirators. Withdrawal is a defense if communicated before the overt act.
